clue.text: Backlash concerning section of the orchestra

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived shorthand for 'concerning', as in a business letter
the percussion section is the drums and cymbals of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A critic complains about the drummers and their part of the orchestra causing a backlash.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is an unwelcome consequence or reaction, just as a backlash is an adverse response.

clue.text: Material that is wrapped around small twig

parts.note: material in the sense of physical, tangible: real

indicators.note: wrapped around says the first piece encloses the second piece placed within it

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Fabric being bound round a slender little twig, as in some craft project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twig' looks like a little branch, but here it is the informal verb meaning to catch on.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British slang for suddenly understanding, which is what it means to realise something.

clue.text: Persistently questions upper-class politicians under pressure

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, says the following letters sit beneath the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the standard physics abbreviation for pressure
U is the old label for upper-class usage in British English
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Posh politicians are put under pressure and keep being questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to quiz them insistently for information, an idiomatic sense of the verb.

clue.text: Turbulent river rose creating large body of water

indicators.note: turbulent water is churned up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A river in spate has risen, forming a great lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake storing a big volume of water for supply.

clue.text: University can upset single person

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Somebody living alone could be thrown by the demands of university life.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is one individual thing or member regarded as a whole, here a lone individual.

clue.text: Dawn reveals this insult about United Nations

indicators.note: about says the first word goes round the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult

explanation.surface: A diplomat named Dawn exposes an insult to the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name; it is daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak brings the first light of the sun, so dawn is when sunshine becomes visible.

clue.text: Sphere of action in government I brought up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gaps

explanation.surface: A politician's area of influence: once in office, they raised it themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TIBRO sits inside 'government I brought', and 'up' turns it round to read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: One's orbit is the range of one's activity or influence, a figurative use of the planetary path.

clue.text: See you scoff very much

parts.note: scoff, as a noun, is informal British for food, which is fare
well means very much, as in 'well over'

explanation.surface: A sneer at someone who mocks a great deal, or a parting greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' looks like the verb to mock; it is British slang for grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are expressions spoken when parting company, so a goodbye is a farewell.

clue.text: Acts to secure son's meals

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the first word grips the letter placed within it

parts.note: feats are notable acts or deeds
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A father performs tricks so his boy gets fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasts are lavish dinners, a grand kind of meal.

clue.text: Simon said strange acknowledgement

indicators.note: strange suggests something out of its normal shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Simon made an odd confession.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is a confession that something is true, so an acknowledgement of it.

clue.text: Prime Minister on the radio? Blast!

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Tony Blair was the British Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007

explanation.surface: A listener curses on hearing a former leader being interviewed on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast!' looks like an exclamation of annoyance; it is the noun meaning a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A blare is a loud, harsh noise such as a trumpet blast.

clue.text: Northern Ireland flipping certain to get guarantee

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so these two letters are read backwards

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A Northern Ireland politician, mildly cursing, is sure to secure a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads as a mild British expletive but turns NI round.
explanation.definitionFit: To insure is to secure against loss, a protective sense close to making a guarantee.

clue.text: Make miserable, good-looking person cut hair

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is chopped off the word

parts.note: a dish is informal for an attractive person
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A handsome man is upset because his hair has been cropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To distress someone is to upset or torment them, causing misery.

clue.text: My boss improved it originally? Only partly

indicators.note: Only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A journalist grumbles that the boss only half improved the first draft.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper writer reports to the editor, who is in charge of the paper; the setter writes for one.

clue.text: Group of soldiers finding young child on railway

parts.note: an infant is a very young child

explanation.surface: A toddler is discovered wandering on the train tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are foot soldiers, a body of troops.

clue.text: Scared small birds

parts.note: chicken is slang for scared or cowardly
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Timid little birds are frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickens are domestic fowl, a type of bird.

clue.text: Red tonic mum's drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mother's gin and tonic has been finished, or a red tonic was drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a common informal term for a communist, from the colour of the movement's flag.

clue.text: Need solid vessel

parts.note: hard means firm or solid
a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a sturdy container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a pot or jug; it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Need here is poverty or want, which is hardship.

clue.text: Relaxed at home with kind American student

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
form means kind or type
L stands for learner, the student driver's plate in the UK

explanation.surface: A US student lounges comfortably at home.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes from the red L plate a British learner driver must display.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual and unceremonious, so laid-back.

clue.text: One new scoop oddly dropped this writer's earnings

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: oddly dropped means the letters in odd positions are discarded, keeping the rest

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as 'this writer', giving ME; the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition

explanation.surface: A journalist's pay fell after a single new scoop came out oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly dropped' removes S, O and P from SCOOP to leave CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money received from work or investment, i.e. one's earnings.

clue.text: What leisurely walker did — risked going topless

indicators.note: going topless means losing its top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: gambled means took a risk

explanation.surface: A daring stroller took a chance by baring all.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, so a leisurely stroller ambled.

clue.text: Bandages doctor, with ease, seems to get cut evenly

indicators.note: cut evenly means the letters in even positions are removed, leaving the odd ones

explanation.surface: A medic bandages a wound easily, which seems to make the cut neat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut evenly' takes the even letters out of EASE SEEMS, leaving ESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress a wound is to bind it, so to bandage it; bandages here is a verb.

clue.text: Wind up judge

definitions.meaning: to wind up a meeting is to bring it to a close
to judge is to reach a verdict or decide

explanation.surface: Tease a court official.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclude means both to finish something and to arrive at a judgement after reasoning.

clue.text: Cowboy may hold this girl with nothing on? On the contrary

indicators.note: On the contrary says the stated order is reversed: the girl goes on top of the nothing, not under it

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cowboy grabs a girl wearing nothing — or rather, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'with nothing on' would put O above LASS; 'On the contrary' sets LASS above O.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a noosed rope a cowboy carries for catching cattle.

clue.text: Soft drink, please — just half

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: just half means only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A customer orders a soft drink but only wants a half measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means pliant and bending easily, so soft rather than stiff.

clue.text: Joanna's leg enthralling a head of orthopaedics

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the first word holds the letter placed within it

parts.note: pins is informal for legs, so a pin is a leg

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A woman named Joanna has a leg that fascinates a senior orthopaedic surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joanna' is Cockney rhyming slang for piano (Joanna rhymes with 'pianner'); the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang, a Joanna is the instrument with keys and hammers.

clue.text: Keeps staring, to an extent — this might attract attention

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone keeps gawping, which might get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is a whispered sound used to catch someone's notice discreetly.

clue.text: Spots 1,000 boats

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
arks are boats, like Noah's

explanation.surface: Someone notices a thousand boats in the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks are stains or blemishes, just as spots are.

clue.text: Doctor has spoilt his places of work

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A medic has wrecked the wards where he is employed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject; it is the verb to tamper, the anagram signal, and 'his' refers back to the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals are where doctors are employed, so a medic's workplaces.

clue.text: First of cigars and old male appeals for matches

indicators.note: First of means the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: petitions are formal appeals or requests

explanation.surface: An elderly man asks first for cigars, then for matches to light them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' suggests things to light a cigar with; it means contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches are sporting contests, a kind of competition.
